title: Retried Redis creation writes can restore consumed one-time records
summary: On Redis, a delayed creation SET may arrive after a retry succeeds and its returned one-time link has already been consumed, restoring the record and its full lifetime. Requires a Redis network interruption and ordering where consumption/state change precedes the delayed write; an ordinary HTTP client cannot trigger it. Redis alone is affected, and another read still requires the full link and applicable authentication.
ai_role: The Yopass maintainer's case-specific security advisory explicitly credits Anthropic's OSS Scanner as discoverer (tracking identifier ANT-2026-MXD9LKP9). It does not name a model version or internal discovery date.
classification_note: The public maintainer advisory documents the finding; it does not establish whether defenders knew of it or whether it was exploited before disclosure.
remediation_note: Yopass 16.0.0 fixes the issue (commit 651006f0105b319cdf6ba44c26579ccdf6c81cb7). Affected-version scope: Versions 14.2.0 through 15.1.0; fixed in 16.0.0 by executing Redis Put SET inside MULTI/EXEC with TxPipelined. An ambiguous failed operation may still have committed server-side. Patch availability does not establish downstream deployment.

impacts.conditions: A Redis retry race can restore a consumed record, violating one-time deletion semantics. The advisory does not claim plaintext access or authentication bypass.
impacts.exploitation: The advisory describes a possible or reproducible trigger as stated; it does not report observed exploitation in the wild.
